main_text.p: „Chanukah, ben Ezekiah, ben Garon scripsere Megillath Thaanith. Hæc sane ex ipso codice satis indicare videntur, opusculum ipsum confectum fuisse ex libro alio sic dicto, in quo dies illi denotantur festi, & ita hoc origines eorum fultus a Thalmudicis explicaret, atque ita Megillah velut Rationarii locum supplerer. Quo quidem, ut argumentum minime leve, [?]spectant, quæ in Gemara Hierosolymitana occurrunt, de [?]cessatione, seu in defuetudinem [?]abitione Megillath Thaanith, quam tangunt, R. Gedaliah ben Jechiel, & R. Asarias Rubeni. Sed vero etiam ante tempus Thalmudis Hierosolymitani laquet notissimum fuisse, eam etiam in defuetudinem [illegible, ~6 letters] seu ullorum, qui illuc [?]sanul ita concurrebant, observationem [?]ex authoritate publica evanuisse. Ubi enim in Gemara illi dies aliquot festi jure supernumerario tantum nixi tractantur (vide ad tit. Thaanoth cap. 2. fol. 66. 1. litt. 13) nec interim observari tunc dicuntur, adjicitur, disciplinam de eis amplexandam fuisse, atque obtinuisse

Quum diu nondum evanuerat [?] abolita est Megillath Thaanith: sed a tempore, quo abolita est Megillath Thaanith (authoritas scilicet ejus omnimoda; licet ob reverentiam legi solerent, & festos dies aliquot, ut dedicationis, Nicanoris, fortium aliudve vim per se retinentes exhiberet) evanuere omnes illi. Ubi R. BA. Tametsi abolita sit Megillath Thaanith, nihilominus Dedicationis festum & illius fortium perpetua manserunt. Tantundem illic, alibique in eâdem

page.notes: Printed quotation marks („) at the start of each line in the left margin are typographic, not text, and are not transcribed. Several words in the blurred centre and lower lines are doubtful and are marked [?]. The bottom of the column is cut off in this part, so the paragraph continues beyond the scan. The remaining readings in the lower-left block are uncertain because of ink show-through and blur. Hebrew lines are set in a block and copied as printed; the blurred final word of the third line is uncertain. The reading of the Latin word after "evanuerat" is doubtful. The italic block is a single paragraph set in italic type.
